pr.title: Teach MIR inliner query cycle avoidance about const_eval_select
pr.author: saethlin

analysis.originalLogic: `mir_inliner_callees` scanned each basic-block terminator and, for `TerminatorKind::Call`, recorded only the directly-called `FnDef`: `if let TerminatorKind::Call { func, .. } = &terminator.kind { let ty = func.ty(&body.local_decls, tcx); let call = match ty.kind() { ty::FnDef(def_id, args) => (*def_id, *args), _ => continue, }; calls.insert(call); }`. Thus the inliner's cycle-avoidance query saw only the immediate callee operand of a call terminator.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: For a call whose direct callee is the `const_eval_select` intrinsic, the query recorded the intrinsic itself (or no useful user-function edge) instead of the function operand passed in the third argument. The recursive f/g edge hidden inside `const_eval_select((), g, g)` was therefore absent from the callee set, so query cycle avoidance could fail to see the mutual recursion.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing `TerminatorKind::Call` terminators, especially calls to `const_eval_select` whose function argument is an `FnDef`; the regression input is a library crate compiled with `-O` containing mutually recursive `#[inline] pub const fn f()`/`g()` that each call `const_eval_select((), other, other)`.
analysis.summary: Bug fix in MIR inliner cycle avoidance: when collecting callees for `mir_inliner_callees`, calls to the `const_eval_select` intrinsic must expose the function operand in `call_args[2]` as the tracked callee, otherwise recursive user functions reached through `const_eval_select` are omitted and the inliner can hit a query cycle. A build-pass `-O` regression test with two mutually recursive const fns through `const_eval_select` was added.
analysis.trigger: Inlining or cycle-avoidance analysis of a call to `const_eval_select` where the actual user function is passed as a function argument rather than being the direct call target, particularly when that function participates in mutual recursion.
preconditions: Index `call_args[2]` is the function operand and its type is also a `ty::FnDef`.
Recursion may be hidden across the function arguments of `const_eval_select`.
pitfalls: Recording only the top-level `FnDef` from a `Call` terminator loses callee edges represented as function arguments.
Cycle avoidance must inspect the function operand in `call_args[2]` for `const_eval_select`; otherwise recursive calls can be missed and query evaluation can cycle.
Do not assume the direct call target is the only relevant callee.
The patch only follows the third argument (`args[2]`), matching the test's runtime-function position.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a compile-only (`//@ build-pass`) UI regression test compiled with `-O --crate-type=lib`, enabling `#![feature(core_intrinsics)]` and `#![feature(const_eval_select)]`, defining mutually recursive `#[inline] pub const fn f()` and `g()` that call `const_eval_select((), g, g)` and `const_eval_select((), f, f)` respectively. A focused test should compare callee-query behavior when the function argument is/is not followed for `const_eval_select`, without requiring execution of the compiled code.
evidence: Teach MIR inliner query cycle avoidance about const_eval_select
